newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France sends more police to riot-torn Guiana.
newsitem.headline: France sends more police to riot-torn Guiana.

text.p: More French police reinforcements arrived in riot-torn French Guiana after violence raged for four nights in a week in Cayenne, the capital, officials said on Thursday.
The French administrator in Guiana, Prefect Pierre Dartout, told a news conference more paramilitary riot police had arrived late on Thursday to patrol the city of 35,000.
"Reinforcements have arrived. We now have proper measures to guarantee the security of persons and property here in Cayenne," Dartout said.
He declined to give numbers but said the police were an addition to reinforcements sent over the weekend.
Paris flew a first contingent of 200 police officers to Cayenne after local police were overwhelmed by the rioting.
While not imposing a formal curfew, officials "recommended" that residents stay off the streets after 10 p.m. on Thursday (0100 GMT on Friday).

"I recommend to the population of Cayenne that it stay off the streets tonight after 10 p.m. This is a recommendation that I am making. I am not imposing a curfew. But as you know, there are groupings that include all types of persons -- vandals but also the curious," Dartout said.

Cayenne has degenerated into a sea of fear and suspicion after four nights of riots killed one person, injured over 20 and caused millions of dollars of damage to property -- mostly government buildings and shops -- in the French territory on the northeastern coast of South America.
Fresh violence erupted in Cayenne for the fourth night in a week late on Wednesday as youths looted stores and clashed with police, witnesses said.

Armed youths erected a barricade on a major boulevard outside the city centre, halting traffic. Police fired tear gas to disperse the crowd, which had robbed stores, set fire to plastic trash cans, burned tires and thrown Molotov cocktail firebombs.
Officials said two police officers were wounded by shotgun fire, most likely from weapons looted from gun stores.
French officials have repeated several times since last week that the violence and looting is well-organised and aims to destabilise French Guiana.
High school students protesting against poor conditions in local schools sparked the riots last week when their strike degenerated into clashes between police and youths.
